post_mortem.lesson: Confusing global user account roles (User RBAC) with contextual committee relationships (Project ABAC) causes critical workflow breakage in academic management systems. Faculty users hold user.role === 'faculty' globally, while their authorization to moderate or view a capstone chapter is determined by their committee appointment on that specific project (project.adviserId, project.panelistIds, project.secretaryId).
post_mortem.learned: Mongoose ObjectIds must always be safely cast to strings (String(project.adviserId) === String(userId)) when performing identity comparisons to avoid silent reference equality failures. Furthermore, optimistic concurrency control via expectedUpdatedAt prevents devastating committee race conditions where multiple panelists review simultaneously.
post_mortem.prevention: Never rely solely on user.role === 'adviser' or user.role === 'panelist' in permission assertion middleware or service layers. Always query the project's committee fields and evaluate role contextually using the standardized helper _isProjectCommitteeMember(project, userId, allowedRoles).
runbook: 1. Verify faculty committee appointment in project document (adviserId, panelistIds, secretaryId).
2. When faculty accesses submission, _assertCanViewSubmission verifies committee membership and grants read access.
3. When faculty submits review, reviewSubmission verifies expectedUpdatedAt matches current submission.updatedAt; if outdated, returns 409 CONCURRENT_REVIEW_CONFLICT.
4. Upon successful moderation, submission.statusHistory records the transition, and notifications are dispatched to all project.memberIds.
